title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a list of research directions begun on the previous page (546). That page summarises how the quantities a, b (here α, β) emerged in the computations from §44 onward and were understood only from §48 III–V, and it states items a) and b). Item a) asks for the class-field-theoretic meaning of these principles over Q(j) (j = e^{2πi/3}) and Q(j'), probably Q(i). Item b) asks for their meaning via the theory of maps (dessins) subordinate to representations of quotients of SL(2,Z)^'.

The overall setting is the 'équation des lacets'. The absolute Galois group Γ_Q acts (outer action) on π̂_1 of M_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} and on related orbifold groups. These include the profinite completion of SL(2,Z)', the commutator subgroup, free of rank 2 and of index 12, identified with π_1 of M_{1,1}' over Q. The elements α, β are cocycle-like parameters of this action. They appear tied to the two orbifold (elliptic) points of M_{1,1} with stabilisers of orders 2 and 3, which correspond to the CM points j = 1728 and j = 0. This is why class field theory of Q(i) and Q(ζ_3) enters.

This page:

c) Endow an object written M_{φ,α} (or M_{g,ν}; the reading is uncertain) with the 'structure elements characteristic of arithmetic Galois groups', for example decomposition and inertia data or Frobenius-type elements. Then relate these to the typical constructions of class field theory, in modern terms CM / Lubin–Tate-type reciprocity at the elliptic points.

d) Ask to what extent one can impose, in this context, the additional compatibility conditions on α, β from §47. These come from compatibility with an isomorphism φ: π̂'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3}, i.e. an identification of the profinite derived/geometric subgroup with the profinite completion of a discrete modular-type group. Grothendieck predicts that the framework of the computations so far is too narrow to incorporate these conditions. These are essentially the GT-type relations (later formalised by Drinfeld/Ihara), here seen through the SL_2 lens.

e) What interests him most is to systematise the preceding computations in a much wider framework than that of the single group SL_2 (written 'SG') and the standard homomorphism. The next page shows this is the homomorphism Ŝ^{+1}_{0,3} → (S)L_2(Ẑ)/±1. There he sketches the programme: obtain 'motivic' representations of Γ_Q by composing the outer Galois action with representations of the discrete group SL(2,Z)' (or SL(2,Z), π_{0,3}) into the Z-points of generically reductive group schemes over Z, then completing profinitely.

So the page is a programmatic plan, not a computation. The plan is to generalise the congruence/standard-representation case (where the Galois action on the SL_2(Ẑ) quotient is governed by the cyclotomic character and CM data) to arbitrary integral representations of the modular group.
errors: No mathematical errors can be checked: the page is programmatic. The forecast in d) (that the framework is too narrow for the extra §47 conditions) is consistent with later knowledge. The standard SL_2(Ẑ) quotient only sees the abelianised/congruence part of the Galois action, roughly the cyclotomic character, and cannot detect the full GT relations.

ideas.what: Relate the parameters α, β of the Galois action on π̂_1(M_{0,3}) / SL(2,Z)^ (tied to the order-2 and order-3 elliptic points) to class field theory, i.e. CM theory of Q(i), Q(ζ_3)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on profinite modular group at elliptic/CM points; tangential base points at CM points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura (Galois action on fundamental groups of modular curves, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in La Longue Marche (1981); not in Esquisse explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: Extra compatibility conditions on (α, β) coming from compatibility with an isomorphism π̂'_{0,3} ≅ completed modular-type group
ideas.modern_name: GT relations (Drinfeld's Grothendieck–Teichmüller group), restricted to the SL_2 / M_{1,1} setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower in general terms

ideas.what: Construct 'motivic' Galois representations by composing the outer Γ_Q-action on π̂_1(M_{1,1}') with representations of SL(2,Z)' into Z-points of reductive group schemes
ideas.modern_name: Galois representations from monodromy of local systems on modular curves / P^1 − 3 points (rigid local systems, motivic local systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (rigid local systems, 1996), Belyi/Thompson rigidity method; Simpson/Esnault–Groechenig on integrality of rigid local systems
ideas.where_published: Ideas in this direction are hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme; detailed form appears only in these notes

missed.claim: A research programme: generalise the explicit Galois computations attached to the standard homomorphism π̂_{0,3}^{+} → SL_2(Ẑ)/±1 to arbitrary integral representations of SL(2,Z)' in generically reductive group schemes, as a systematic source of motivic Γ_Q-representations, and make explicit how the GT-type parameters (α, β) behave there.
missed.quote: Ce qui m'intéresse le plus pour le moment, c'est une systématisation des calculs précédents dans un cadre beaucoup plus vaste que celui du seul groupe SG et de l'hom. standard
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links the GT/anabelian programme to the modern theory of motivic and rigid local systems on modular curves and to non-congruence subgroups. That theory came later (Katz, Esnault–Groechenig, Litt) and mostly without reference to the GT parametrisation.

missed.claim: Linking the Galois parameters α, β at the two elliptic points with class field theory (CM by Q(i), Q(ζ_3)) and asking to introduce Frobenius/reciprocity structure on the relevant moduli object.
missed.quote: Introduire sur M_{φ,α} les éléments de structure caractéristiques des groupes de Galois arithmétiques — et faire le lien avec les constructions typiques de cet ordre en théorie des corps de classes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is partially realised by work on Galois actions at CM tangential base points (Ihara, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto on universal mixed elliptic motives). The explicit class-field-theoretic interpretation of the GT-parameters at j = 0, 1728 is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A programmatic page; its broad ideas (GT relations, Galois action on the modular group, motivic representations from π_1) are known themes. The specific plan to use integral representations of SL(2,Z)' into reductive group schemes as a systematic machine for motivic Γ_Q-representations, tied to CM class field theory at the elliptic points, is a notable unpublished detail but not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: Item c): the image reads 'Introduire sur M_{φ,α}' (subscripts resembling φ, α), not 'M_{g,u}'. A reading M_{g,ν} remains possible but less likely given the α, β, φ context.
Item d): '— y prévoir d'ailleurs' should probably be '— je prévois d'ailleurs'.
Item e): 'l'hom. Stainhaus' is very likely 'l'hom. standard' (the standard homomorphism to SL_2(Ẑ)/±1, continued on the next page). 'SG' is plausibly 'SL_2'.
